_note: Written originally for this site. It was prompted by the TRREB 'Whose Job Is It?' sheets the client supplied, but NONE of that document's content is reproduced: those sheets were last updated in December 2015 and their phone numbers are a decade old. Publishing stale service numbers would be worse than publishing nothing. What is genuinely durable is the structure, which is that York and Durham split services between the regional and the local municipality, and that knowing which tier owns a problem saves a wasted call. Contact URLs below are municipal front doors rather than deep links, because those move.
_instructions: Check each URL resolves before launch and set _links_verified to true.
intro: Ontario outside Toronto runs on two tiers of municipal government, and new owners lose a lot of time calling the wrong one. In York and Durham the region handles water, wastewater and waste collection, while your own town or city handles roads, parking, by-law enforcement, building permits and property tax. Toronto is a single tier, so everything goes through 311.

tiers.name: The region
owns: Drinking water supply and water quality
Waste collection, recycling and green bin
Regional roads, usually the numbered ones
tiers.note: If the problem is what comes out of the tap or what gets picked up at the curb, it is almost always regional.

tiers.name: Your town or city
tiers.applies_to: Markham, Richmond Hill, Vaughan, Ajax, Pickering, Whitby and the rest
owns: Local roads, sidewalks and snow clearing
Water and sewer billing in some municipalities
tiers.note: Anything about the property itself, or the street in front of it, starts here.

tiers.name: Toronto
tiers.note: Toronto amalgamated the two tiers. Call 311 and they route it.

before_you_call.title: Have the roll number ready
before_you_call.body: Your property tax roll number identifies the property faster than the address, and it is on your tax bill.

before_you_call.title: Check whether it is on your side of the line
before_you_call.body: The municipality maintains the water main and the sewer in the street. The service connection from there into your house is usually yours, and that division decides who pays.

before_you_call.title: Permits are cheaper than remediation
before_you_call.body: Work done without a permit surfaces on resale, and an open permit or an unpermitted alteration can hold up a closing. Ask before the work, not after.

before_you_call.title: Locates are free and legally required
before_you_call.body: Before any digging, request utility locates through Ontario One Call. Hitting a gas or hydro line is the expensive way to learn this.
